title: PHTI Releases Landmark Framework to Scale High-Value Clinical AI Over Administrative Waste
key_facts: PHTI released a framework for scaling clinical AI that helps patients over AI that mainly handles administration.
It says an AI scribe raised high-complexity Level 5 visits by 5% and Level 4 visits by 7% for established patients, adding an average of $1,004 per doctor per month in billing.
Insurers use their own algorithms to downcode, audit and deny claims, creating an 'AI vs AI' fight.
It argues for outcome-based payment, citing the CMS Innovation Center's ACCESS model launched mid-2026, and for payment that falls as software scales.
It calls for clearer liability rules for autonomous AI, citing the Utah AI regulatory sandbox and the FDA's TEMPO pilot.
Three in four diagnosed hypertension patients do not have blood pressure under control, the article says.
PHTI executive director Caroline Pearson says the systems are not yet in place to deliver the benefits.
quote_evidence: PHTI’s blueprint—hammered out alongside hospital executives, top health plans, tech pioneers, and federal regulators at CMS, the FDA, and ARPA-H—argues that policymakers must stop treating healthcare AI like a technological problem and start treating it as a payment design problem.

“While this technology has the potential to improve patients’ health, make care more accessible and convenient, and increase affordability, we don’t currently have the systems in place to achieve that vision.”
why_it_matters_hint: The way US healthcare pays for care may push AI toward billing tasks instead of better health.
notes: The article is written in an opinionated style and relays PHTI's report; PHTI's full report was not read.
